conviction_note: The $372m market cap is a price collapse, not a corporate action: spot $8.83 x ~43.2m diluted shares (Q2 net loss $31.1m / $0.72 per share) is about $380m, 76% off the 52w high, after two guidance resets (Feb -10.8%, May -20.7%) and a Q2 with 6.6% gross margin. The FY26 guide ($775-800m revenue, $0-10m adj EBITDA) needs H2 revenue of at least $421.8m against H1 $353.2m, which the ~$182m Q3 consensus does not reach, so a cut looks close to certain and largely expected. Against that sit a ~20% short float, a take-private report (Axios, 16 Sep) the stock has given back 20% since, and company velocity data improving into July. The findings net to about zero, p_up 48 on a 17% absolute move.
bar: DISPUTED. Q3 revenue: ~$182m and EPS ~($0.14) per the sweep's aggregator row (searcher-briefs/VITL.json). Earnings Whispers shows EPS ($0.13) and revenue ~$199.8m (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/VITL); the $199.8m is likely stale because it roughly equals Q3 2025's $198.9m. The two sources agree on EPS (about -$0.13 to -$0.14), not on revenue. The company guide is the firmer bar: FY26 net revenue $775-800m, adj EBITDA $0-10m, capex $70-75m, reaffirmed 2026-08-06 on the assumption that 'category price levels remain stabilized at current levels' and that shell egg volume returns to growth in H2 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001579733/000119312526336692/vitl-ex99_1.htm). H1 revenue was $353.2m (Q1 ~$187.2m, Q2 $166.0m), so the low end of the guide needs H2 >= $421.8m. Findings that depend on the revenue consensus are capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 8.7M shares, 20.4% of float, 6.1 days to cover, settlement 2026-08-20, per Equibles (https://equibles.com/stocks/vitl/shortinterest). FINRA via Curved Trading: 8.0M shares, 5.1 days at 2026-07-15. MarketBeat (Oct 2026 page) shows ~21% of float, recently down 16.9%. AltIndex shows 10.46M, 24.35% of shares outstanding, undated. findings.finding: The reaffirmed FY26 guide of $775-800m revenue needs H2 revenue of at least $421.8m (H1 was $353.2m). The ~$182m Q3 consensus would leave Q4 needing about $240m or more, against Q3 2025's $198.9m peak quarter. The adj EBITDA guide of $0-10m sits on an H1 that includes a -$26.6m Q2. A cut to both lines on this print is very likely, and the sell-side bar already sits below the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is what moves this stock. Feb 2026 (weak FY26 guide, $910m midpoint vs consensus) -10.8%; May 2026 (guide cut to $775-800m, butter exit) -20.7%; Aug 2026 (guide reaffirmed after a 6.6% gross margin quarter) +2.2%; Dec 2025 investor-day trim about -9%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Consensus Q3 revenue (~$182m) already implies a full year below the $775m low end, the stock is 76% off its high, and analysts cut targets in late October (TD Cowen to $8, DA Davidson on 27 Oct). If a cut were fully priced, the stock would not have reacted +2.2% to the August reaffirmation. What is unpriced is the size of the new range and whether the EBITDA guide goes negative.
findings.independence: The Barchart piece of 2026-08-06 called the full-year sales guide 'optimistic' (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3691874/vital-farms-nasdaqvitl-surprises-with-q2-cy2026-sales-full-year-sales-guidance-is-optimistic). This finding shares the company document with the financing finding.

findings.finding: Cal-Maine, the largest US egg producer, reported its quarter ended 2026-08-29 (overlapping two-thirds of VITL's Q3, 29 Jun-27 Sep) on 2026-09-30. Specialty shell egg sales fell 14.0%: average selling price per dozen -10.7%, volume -3.8%. Specialty segment income fell to $14.9m from $64.2m. Conventional ASP fell 59.3%. VITL's guide assumes shell egg volume returns to growth in H2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue -10.1% YoY, attributed to oversupply and breaker sales, bought +2.2% because the guide held. Earlier volume misses came with guide cuts (-20.7% May 2026).
findings.why_not_priced: A peer that reported after VITL last spoke (6 Aug). It is a proxy: Cal-Maine's specialty mix is cage-free-heavy, not pasture-raised. If the market had fully read it across, VITL's Q3 consensus would sit below Q2's $166m, not at ~$182m.
findings.independence: Proxy, counterparty peer. Corroborated by https://www.thepoultrysite.com/news/2026/10/cal-maine-foods-swings-to-loss-in-first-quarter-of-fiscal-2027 (same Cal-Maine release, so not independent of it).

findings.finding: USDA wholesale data for October 2026: caged Large eggs delivered to warehouses at 51-76 cents per dozen (week of 11-17 Oct), National Large loose at 46 cents (week of 2 Oct), shell egg inventory up 3.6% week on week (12 Oct report), layer flock 311.7M. The commodity price gap to Vital Farms (~$8.16 per retail unit in Q2) stays extreme, and breaker and wholesale disposal of excess eggs, which cost $19.5m of Q2 gross profit, stays uneconomic.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The oversupply-driven Q2 margin collapse (38.9% to 6.6%) was looked through on a held guide (+2.2%).
findings.why_not_priced: Public commodity series. Its bearing on the Q4 guide depends on whether prices are below the 'current levels' the August guide assumed, which I could not establish. If commodity pressure were fully priced, the take-private premium would not need to be discounted further.
findings.independence: Macro-to-company transmission. Cal-Maine's CEO on 2026-09-30 said conventional pricing 'remains under pressure from an industry supply imbalance' (https://www.thepoultrysite.com/news/2026/10/cal-maine-foods-swings-to-loss-in-first-quarter-of-fiscal-2027).

findings.finding: The company's September 2026 investor presentation shows its price-gap cuts working into Q3, all from Circana. Average weekly volume per store selling per item recovered from 24 (4 weeks to 19 Apr) to 27 (building, 19 Jul), +12.5%. At a top-10 retailer the price gap narrowed from $1.79 to $0.27, with units per store per week +27% and new households +27.2%. The Q4'26 TDP estimate is 170-175, against 150-160 for the full year and 130 in 2025.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Aug 2026 print, where management called Q2 the trough and reaffirmed the guide on distribution gains, bought +2.2%. Q3 2025 (beat, held guide) +16.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: Company-published but promotional, and it stops in July. The stock fell from ~$10-11 to $8.83 after it was published, so the market is not crediting a velocity recovery. If it were, Q3 consensus would sit well above the guide-implied path rather than below it.
findings.independence: The Q2 release says retail dollar share grew more than 200bp (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001579733/000119312526336692/vitl-ex99_1.htm). Same company, so not independent. Cal-Maine's specialty volume -3.8% points the other way at category level.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-16 Axios reported that Vital Farms is weighing strategic alternatives including a take-private. Shares rose 8.3% to $11.08, and StoneX cited a $15-25 per share range. The stock has since fallen to $8.83 (-20%). No company statement or 8-K has followed; EDGAR shows no 8-K since 17 Aug. Management may address it or decline to on the 3 Nov call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: One observation: the Axios report itself bought +8.3% intraday on 2026-09-17, and all of it was given back within a month.
findings.why_not_priced: Priced at close to zero: the stock is below the pre-report level. A formal review announcement or a sale process would reprice it toward the $15-25 range. A denial costs little, because the premium is already gone. Asymmetric, low probability.
findings.independence: German coverage of the same Axios report (https://stock3.com/news/vital-farms-going-private-geruecht-trifft-auf-ein-angeschlagenes-ei-17290228). It is the same underlying report, so not independent.

findings.finding: Liquidity has tightened. Cash was $21.2m at 28 Jun (down from $51.4m at end of Q1, with no debt then), $30m is drawn, H1 operating cash flow was -$45.9m and H1 capex $37.5m against a FY capex guide of $70-75m. New $125m 3-year term loan plus $60m ABL. The buyback was terminated on 3 Aug 'consistent with the terms of the new lending facilities'. The money funds capex (processing capacity at VXR, Indiana) and operating losses, not a corroborated demand ramp, because volume is declining.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The facilities were announced with the Q2 print (+2.2%), so the market read them as removing a near-term liquidity question rather than as distress.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q3 balance sheet and cash burn are first visible on 3 Nov. A capex cut would be positive for cash. Further burn with the term-loan draw rising would feed the distress narrative. Small either way.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 cash of $51.4m with no debt, per the 8-K summary at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001579733/000119312526210294/vitl-ex99_1.htm. Shares a document with the guidance finding.

findings.finding: Short interest is crowded at about 20-24% of float with 5-6 days to cover (8.7M shares, 20.4% of float, 6.1 days at 2026-08-20). Any print that is less bad than feared (a guide cut smaller than consensus already implies, Q3 margin recovery, capex cut, a strategic-review update) meets forced covering.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 +16.1% and Q2 2025 +17.6% on relief prints. Aug 2026 +2.2% on a bad quarter with a held guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is a mechanism rather than an unpriced fact. The +4 skew shows the option market leaning to downside while a fifth of the float is short; if relief were priced, short interest would have been covered into the print.
findings.independence: MarketBeat ~21% of float (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/vital-farms-nasdaqvitl-director-buys-9225000-in-stock-2026-03-11/); FINRA via Curved Trading 8.0M at 2026-07-15 (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/vitl/short-interest/).

findings.finding: The butter business is being wound down by fiscal year end: $7.8m of exit costs in Q2 and $2.1m of assets held for sale. Further exit costs will sit in Q3 and are excluded from adjusted numbers.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Announced with the May 2026 guide cut (-20.7%), where the guide dominated.
findings.why_not_priced: Known since May and below adjusted EBITDA, with no path to the guide beyond removing a small loss-making line. Sized at zero.
findings.independence: Boerse Express, butter production ended by end 2026 (https://www.boerse-express.com/news/articles/vital-farms-aktie-buttergeschaeft-bis-ende-2026-weg-923576).

findings.finding: The sell-side bar was cut into the print: TD Cowen cut its target to $8.00 (October, per the rava feed) and DA Davidson cut on 27 Oct, citing execution risk. Yahoo's 27 Oct preview headline was 'Q3 earnings expected to decline'. Expectations were lowered in the final week.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean prior; Aug 2026 came in near a reset bar and bought +2.2%.
findings.why_not_priced: Target cuts are wire copy and largely priced. Their only edge is that a lowered bar makes a cut that lands inside consensus-implied numbers less damaging.

outside_window.finding: Shareholder class action and law-firm investigations (Bronstein Gewirtz, 2026-10-25) alleging misleading statements on the ERP rollout. They resolve over months, not in the window.

baseline_tension: The negatives (guide gap, peer specialty volume, commodity oversupply) agree with the +4 put skew and are probably mostly priced. The crowded short, the discarded take-private premium and the company's own velocity data cut against the skew. Net about zero, so p_up sits near 50 with a slight lean to the skew.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (a crowded short shrinks negatives; ~20-24% of float short): guide-gap finding -2.0 to -1.5, Cal-Maine proxy -1.5 to -1.2, USDA commodity proxy -1.0 to -0.8

Rule 4 (financing is a question): asked what the $185m buys. It funds capex and operating losses with volume declining, not a ramp. Kept at -0.5, small, since the August market read it as liquidity relief
Rule 6 (disputed bar): the revenue consensus is disputed (182 vs 199.8), so the guide-gap finding rests on company H1 numbers and the guide instead; p_up moved from 47 to 48
Rules 2 and 5 left the butter one-off at 0 and the proxies small, already sized that way; nothing dropped
